description.en: The Hebrew word “kabbalah” means “receiving,” and it has multiple specific associations in different contexts. It is often used to refer to a “received” tradition, passed down through generations. In particular in classic rabbinic sources it refers to the [Prophets](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Tanakh/Prophets) and the [Writings](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Tanakh/Writings), the parts of the [Hebrew Bible](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Tanakh) other than the five books of the Torah. Nowadays, it is most often used to refer to [Jewish mysticism](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Kabbalah), and sometimes to a particular school of Jewish mysticism that began in Western Europe in the middle ages and spread and evolved throughout the Jewish world.
